items.title: Newtonian stress and Fourier conductive closure
items.design_state: Step 1 draft authored; readiness recorded separately.
items.physical_scope: An adopted smooth, isotropic, single-component Newtonian/Fourier closure with specified state laws, nonnegative shear and bulk coefficients, and positive-semidefinite symmetric conductivity part. No coefficient is inferred from a measurement and no universal fluid applicability is asserted.
items.statement: Use a Cartesian inertial frame in Newtonian spacetime. At an event let $u$ be the fluid velocity, $T>0$ its temperature, $\rho>0$ its mass density, and $\xi=(\rho,T)$ its local state in a specified open set $\mathcal S\subset(0,\infty)^2$. The velocity gradient has components $L_{ij}=\partial_{x_j}u_i$; define the symmetric rate matrix $D=(L+L^T)/2$, its trace $\theta=\operatorname{tr}D$, and its trace-free part $D_0=D-\theta I_3/3$, where $I_3$ is the $3\times3$ identity matrix. For $A,B\in\mathbb R^{3\times3}$, use the Frobenius contraction $A:B=\sum_{i,j=1}^3A_{ij}B_{ij}$.

items.title: Positive-response linear sound in adopted barotropic fluid
items.design_state: Step 1 draft authored; readiness recorded separately.
items.physical_scope: First variation about a uniform rest state of the adopted smooth, positive-density barotropic model when its pressure law is the fixed-entropy restriction of the adopted local state relation. The prediction is linear; no finite-amplitude error, lifespan, material measurement or empirical sound-speed claim is asserted.
items.statement: Let $I\subset\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open time interval and $\Omega\subset I\times\mathbb R^3$ a nonempty open domain for the model fields. Let $e\in C^2(\mathcal U)$ be the local specific-energy relation on an open $\mathcal U\subset(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R$, with state coordinates $(v,s)$, $T=e_s$, and $p=-e_v$; each state partial derivative holds the other coordinate fixed. Fix $(v_b,s_b)\in\mathcal U$ with $T_b>0$ and $e_{ss}(v_b,s_b)>0$, set $\rho_b=1/v_b$, and take the barotropic pressure law to be $P(\rho)=p(1/\rho,s_b)$ near $\rho_b$. This is the fixed-entropy restriction of the adopted local state relation. The smooth barotropic Euler model is linearized about the uniform rest state $(\rho,u)=(\rho_b,0)$. items.title: Closed smooth incompressible kinetic-energy dissipation
items.design_state: Step 1 draft authored; readiness recorded separately.
items.physical_scope: Conditional kinetic-energy identity for an actual smooth unforced, constant-density incompressible Newtonian solution on a fixed no-slip domain or periodic domain. It asserts no existence, uniqueness, long-time regularity, global solution or empirical realization.
items.statement: Let $I\subset\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open time interval containing $0$. Suppose a smooth solution of the constant-density incompressible Newtonian model has $\rho=\rho_0>0$, $\operatorname{div}u=0$, constant $\mu\ge0$, zero body force, and stress $\sigma=-pI_3+2\mu D$. Assume the complete $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, smooth-motion, positive-density, contact/stress-regularity, continuity, and separate linear/angular-momentum and total-energy balance hypotheses of the mathematical local-balance equivalence result, as specified in Facts & Assumptions. The spatial region is either a nonempty bounded $C^1$ domain fixed in time with no-slip condition $u=0$ on its boundary, or a periodic domain with the fields and their derivatives periodic on opposite faces of a rectangular period cell with positive side lengths. For the periodic case, interpret the local balance assumptions on the periodic lift to $\mathbb R^3$.

items.title: Negative bulk viscosity violates entropy admissibility
items.design_state: Step 1 draft authored; readiness recorded separately.
items.physical_scope: Algebraic counterexample in the Newtonian/Fourier residual family with negative bulk coefficient. This coefficient lies outside the adopted nonnegative-bulk postulate; the example is not a material observation or claim about a realized fluid.
items.statement: Within the smooth compressible Newtonian/Fourier residual family, a nonnegative shear viscosity $\mu\ge0$ by itself guarantees nonnegative local entropy production for every $T>0$, every symmetric rate matrix $D$, and every temperature gradient $g\in\mathbb R^3$, regardless of the bulk coefficient $\zeta$.

items.title: Negative acoustic response yields exponential mode growth
items.design_state: Step 1 draft authored; readiness recorded separately.
items.physical_scope: Exact counterexample for the linearized equations of an explicitly adopted smooth barotropic state relation with negative fixed-entropy pressure response. It is not a finite-amplitude solution or an empirical claim about a realized material.
items.statement: For every smooth positive-density barotropic rest state with negative fixed-entropy pressure response $P'(\rho_b)<0$, all smooth solutions of its first-variation system remain bounded in time.
